readings.title: A Secret Meeting
readings.subtitle: David and Jonathan Consult
readings.text: [1 Samuel 20:1] And Dawiḏ fled from Nayoth in Ramah, and came and said before Yonathan, “What have I done? What is my crookedness, and what is my sin before your father, that he seeks <dn>את</dn> my life?” [2] And he said to him, “Far from it! You do not die! See, my father does nothing great or small except he discloses it to me. And why should my father hide <dn>את</dn> this matter from me? It is not so!” [3] But Dawiḏ swore again, and said, “Your father certainly knows that I have found favor in your eyes, and he says, ‘Let not Yonathan know this, lest he be grieved.’ But truly, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> lives and as your soul lives, there is but a step between me and death.” [4] And Yonathan said to Dawiḏ, “Whatever your soul says, I do for you.” [5] And Dawiḏ said to Yonathan, “See, tomorrow is the New Moon, and I ought to sit with the sovereign to eat. But let me go, and I shall hide myself in the field until the third evening. [6] “If your father at all misses me, then say, ‘Dawiḏ earnestly asked leave of me to run to Běyth Leḥem, his city, for there is a yearly slaughtering there for all the clan.’ [7] “If he says thus, ‘It is well,’ your servant has peace. But if he is very wroth, then know that evil is decided by him. [8] “And you shall show kindness to your servant, for you have brought <dn>את</dn> your servant into a covenant of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> with you. And if there is crookedness in me, kill me yourself, for why should you bring me to your father?” [9] And Yonathan said, “Far be it from you! For if I certainly knew that evil was decided by my father to come upon you, would I not make <dn>את</dn> it known to you?” [10] And Dawiḏ said to Yonathan, “Who would make it known to me, or what if your father answers you harshly?” [11] And Yonathan said to Dawiḏ, “Come, and let us go out into the field.” So both of them went out into the field.

readings.title: The Covenant and the Sign
readings.subtitle: The Arrow of YeHoVaH's Deliverance
readings.text: [1 Samuel 20:12] And Yonathan said to Dawiḏ, “<dn>YeHoVaH Elohim</dn> of Yisra’el is witness! When I have searched out <dn>את</dn> my father sometime tomorrow, or the third day, and see, if there is good toward Dawiḏ, and I do not then send to you and disclose <dn>את</dn> it to you, [13] “let <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> do so and much more to Yonathan. But if it pleases my father to do you <dn>את</dn> evil, then I shall disclose <dn>את</dn> it to you and send you away, and you shall go in peace. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> be with you as <dn>He</dn> has been with my father. [14] “And stay alive, not only while I live, show me the kindness of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, that I do not die, [15] but also do not cut off <dn>את</dn> your kindness from my house forever, no, not when <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has cut off <dn>את</dn> every one of the enemies of Dawiḏ from the face of the earth.” [16] Thus Yonathan made a covenant with the house of Dawiḏ, saying, “Let <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> require it at the hand of Dawiḏ’s enemies.” [17] And Yonathan again made <dn>את</dn> Dawiḏ swear, because he loved him, for he loved him as he loved his own soul. [18] And Yonathan said to him, “Tomorrow is the New Moon, and you shall be missed, because your seat shall be empty. [19] “And when you have stayed three days, go down quickly and come to the place where you hid on the day of the deed, and remain by the stone Ezal. [20] “And I am going to shoot three arrows to the side of it, as though I shot at a target. [21] “And see, I shall send <dn>את</dn> the youth, saying, ‘Go, find <dn>את</dn> the arrows.’ If I explicitly say to the youth, ‘Look, the arrows are on this side of you, get them,’ then come, for there is peace for you and no matter, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> lives. [22] “But if I say thus to the young man, ‘Look, the arrows are beyond you,’ go, for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has sent you away. [23] “And as for the matter which you and I have spoken of, see, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is between you and me forever.”

readings.title: The King's Fury
readings.subtitle: Saul Attempts to Kill Jonathan
readings.text: [1 Samuel 20:24] So Dawiḏ hid in the field. And when the New Moon came, the sovereign sat down to eat <dn>את</dn> the food. [25] And the sovereign sat on his seat, as at other times, on a seat by the wall, and Yonathan arose, and Aḇněr sat by Sha’ul’s side, but Dawiḏ’s place was empty. [26] And Sha’ul spoke nothing that day, for he thought, “It is an accident, he is not clean, for he has not been cleansed.” [27] And it came to be the next day, the second day of the month, that Dawiḏ’s place was empty. And Sha’ul said to Yonathan his son, “Why has the son of Yishai not come to eat, either yesterday or today?” [28] And Yonathan answered <dn>את</dn> Sha’ul, “Dawiḏ earnestly asked leave of me to go to Běyth Leḥem. [29] “And he said, ‘Please let me go, for our clan has a slaughtering in the city, and my brother has commanded me to be there. And now, if I have found favor in your eyes, please let me get away and see <dn>את</dn> my brothers.’ Therefore he has not come to the sovereign’s table.” [30] And the displeasure of Sha’ul burned against Yonathan, and he said to him, “You son of a perverse, rebellious woman! Do I not know that you have chosen the son of Yishai to your own shame and to the shame of your mother’s nakedness? [31] “For as long as the son of Yishai lives on the earth, you are not established, nor your reign. And now, send and bring <dn>את</dn> him to me, for he is a son of death!” [32] And Yonathan answered <dn>את</dn> Sha’ul his father, and said to him, “Why should he be put to death? What has he done?” [33] And Sha’ul hurled <dn>את</dn> a spear at him to smite him, then Yonathan knew that it was decided by his father to kill <dn>את</dn> Dawiḏ. [34] So Yonathan rose from the table in burning displeasure, and ate no food the second day of the month, for he was grieved for Dawiḏ, because his father had put him to shame.

readings.title: The Final Farewell
readings.subtitle: Jonathan and David Part Ways
readings.text: [1 Samuel 20:35] And it came to be in the morning, that Yonathan went out into the field at the time appointed with Dawiḏ, and a small youth was with him. [36] And he said to his youth, “Now run, find <dn>את</dn> the arrows which I shoot.” As the youth ran, he shot an arrow beyond him. [37] And when the youth came to the place where the arrow which Yonathan had shot fell, Yonathan called after the youth and said, “Is not the arrow beyond you?” [38] And Yonathan called after the youth, “Make haste, hurry, do not stand still!” And Yonathan’s youth gathered up <dn>את</dn> the arrows and came to his master. [39] But the youth knew nothing, only Yonathan and Dawiḏ knew <dn>את</dn> the matter. [40] And Yonathan gave <dn>את</dn> his weapons to his youth, and said to him, “Go, take them to the city.” [41] As soon as the youth had gone, Dawiḏ arose from the south side, and fell on his face to the ground, and bowed three times. And they kissed one another, and they wept together, until Dawiḏ exceeded. [42] And Yonathan said to Dawiḏ, “Go in peace, since we both have sworn in the Name of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, saying, ‘<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is between me and you, and between my seed and your seed, forever.’ ” Then he arose and departed, and Yonathan went into the city.

readings.title: David at Nob
readings.subtitle: The Bread of the Presence
readings.text: [1 Samuel 21:1] And Dawiḏ came to Noḇ, to Aḥimeleḵ the priest. And Aḥimeleḵ was afraid at the meeting of Dawiḏ, and said to him, “Why are you alone, and no one with you?” [2] And Dawiḏ said to Aḥimeleḵ the priest, “The sovereign has commanded me a matter, and said to me, ‘Let no one know anything of <dn>את</dn> the matter about which I send you, and which I have commanded you.’ And I have directed my young men to such and such a place. [3] “And now, what is under your hand? Give me five loaves of bread in my hand, or whatever is found.” [4] And the priest answered <dn>את</dn> Dawiḏ and said, “There is no ordinary bread under my hand, but there is set-apart bread, provided the young men have kept themselves from women.” [5] And Dawiḏ answered <dn>את</dn> the priest and said to him, “Truly, women have been kept from us about three days since I came out. And the vessels of the young men are set-apart, and it is an ordinary journey, and how much more set-apart is the bread in the vessels today?” [6] So the priest gave him set-apart bread, for there was no bread there but the showbread which had been taken from before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, to put on hot bread on the day it was taken away. [7] And a certain man of the servants of Sha’ul was there that day, detained before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. And his name was Do’ěḡ, an Eḏomite, the chief of the herdsmen of Sha’ul. [8] And Dawiḏ said to Aḥimeleḵ, “And is there not here under your hand a spear or a sword? For I have brought neither my sword nor my weapons with me, because the sovereign’s matter was urgent.” [9] And the priest said, “The sword of Golyath the Philistine, whom you smote in the Valley of Elah, see, it is wrapped in a cloth behind the ephoḏ. If you wish to take that for yourself, take it. For there is no other except that here.” And Dawiḏ said, “There is none like it, give it to me.”

readings.title: David in Gath
readings.subtitle: Fleeing from Saul to the Philistines
readings.text: [1 Samuel 21:10] And Dawiḏ arose and fled that day from before Sha’ul, and went to Aḵish the sovereign of Gath. [11] And the servants of Aḵish said to him, “Is this not Dawiḏ the sovereign of the land? Did they not sing of him to one another in dances, saying, ‘Sha’ul has smitten his thousands, and Dawiḏ his ten thousands’?” [12] And Dawiḏ took <dn>את</dn> these words to heart, and was very much afraid of Aḵish the sovereign of Gath. [13] So he changed <dn>את</dn> his behavior before them, and feigned madness in their hands, and scratched on the doors of the gate, and let his spittle run down on his beard. [14] And Aḵish said to his servants, “Look, you see <dn>את</dn> the man is mad. Why do you bring him to me? [15] “Do I lack madmen, that you have brought <dn>את</dn> this one to act as a madman before me? Should this one come into my house?”

readings.title: A Song of Deliverance
readings.subtitle: David Praises YeHoVaH for Safety
readings.text: [Psalm 34:1] I bless <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> at all times; <dn>His</dn> praise is continually in my mouth. [2] My soul boasts in <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>; Let the humble hear and be glad. [3] Oh, make <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> great with me, And let us exalt <dn>His</dn> Name together. [4] I sought <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and <dn>He</dn> answered me, And delivered me from all my fears. [5] They looked to <dn>Him</dn> and were enlightened, And their faces were not ashamed. [6] This poor man cried out and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> heard him, And saved him out of all his adversities. [7] The messenger of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> encamps all around those who fear <dn>Him</dn>, And rescues them. [8] Oh, taste and see that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is good; Blessed is the man who takes refuge in <dn>Him</dn>! [9] Fear <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, you <dn>His</dn> set-apart ones, For there is no lack to those who fear <dn>Him</dn>. [10] Young lions have lacked and been hungry; But those who seek <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> lack no good matter. [11] Come, you children, listen to me; Let me teach you the fear of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [12] Who is the man who desires life, Who loves many days, in order to see good? [13] Keep your tongue from evil, And your lips from speaking deceit. [14] Turn away from evil and do good; Seek peace and pursue it. [15] The eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> are on the righteous, And <dn>His</dn> ears are open to their cry. [16] The face of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is against evil-doers, To cut off their remembrance from the earth. [17] The righteous cried out, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> heard, And delivered them out of all their adversities. [18] <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is near to the broken-hearted, And saves <dn>את</dn> those whose spirit is crushed. [19] Many are the evils of the righteous, But <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> delivers him out of them all. [20] <dn>He</dn> is guarding all his bones; Not one of them is broken. [21] Evil slays the wrong, And those who hate the righteous are guilty. [22] <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> redeems the soul of <dn>His</dn> servants, And none of those taking refuge in <dn>Him</dn> are guilty.
